standard_prerequisites.name: For a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes the direct image preserves quasi-coherence, whence the restriction functor on quasi-coherent modules to an affine open of a quasi-separated scheme is essentially surjective
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the vanishing condition from X to the affine open U.

standard_prerequisites.name: On an affine open the derived quasi-coherent object corresponds to a complex of modules over the ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the tor amplitude to the module level.

standard_prerequisites.name: A complex of modules whose derived tensor products with all modules have cohomology in a fixed range has tor amplitude in that range, by the affine tor dimension lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes the affine case and the lemma.

core_obligations: Direction (1) implies (2) is immediate from the definition of tor amplitude (proof line 2613).

Reduction to affines: for an affine open U of the quasi-separated X, the inclusion j : U -> X is quasi-compact separated, so j_* preserves quasi-coherence and the restriction functor QCoh(O_X) -> QCoh(O_U) is essentially surjective; hence the vanishing in (2) implies the analogous vanishing on U for all quasi-coherent G (proof lines 2615-2623).

Affine case: write U = Spec(A) and let M^bullet be the complex corresponding to E|_U by the affine comparison; the transferred vanishing says M^bullet tensor^L N has cohomology only in [a, b] for all modules N, i.e. M^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b]; by the affine tor dimension lemma E|_U has tor amplitude in [a, b], and since affine opens cover X the object E has tor amplitude in [a, b] (proof lines 2624-2632).
proof_roadmap: Transfer the vanishing to affine opens via essential surjectivity of the restriction (proof lines 2615-2623).
Conclude on affines by the module-level tor amplitude criterion (proof lines 2624-2632).
